jobs.description:
A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials at the interface between materials science and synthetic biology, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. The multidisciplinary component of our research requires intensive information and data exchange between multiple disciplines. We work on semantically structured data and interfaces, AI-driven workflows, and contribute to engaging the growing ELM community in digitalized research.

To support the digitalization of SynBio work within the context of ELM development, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Synthetic Biology (f/m/d)

and interest in data-driven research. The position is integrated in the collaborative network MaterialVital Hub, recently funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) in collaboration with the Galaxy Community Hub. The candidate will be part of a team of experimental scientists and research data management experts at INM-Leibniz Institute for New Materials and Bioinformaticians at the University of Freiburg.

Your roles:

- Contribute to the digitalization of synthetic biology workflows for ELM development in collaboration with SynBio researchers at INM.
- Develop metadata schemas for typical synthetic biology steps and methodologies in ELM research which are transferable to electronic LabBooks and data platforms of relevance for other researchers within the MaterialVital Hub.
- Contribute to the development of an ELM-dedicated ontology for interoperability within the MaterialVital Hub in cooperation with MaterialDigital Platform partners and the Galaxy Community Hub.
- Support and promote digitalization of the ELM community within the MaterialVital Hub in close interaction with Galaxi Community Hub and MaterialDigital Platform and NFDI.
- Attend workshops and disseminate your work within the ELM community by presenting at conferences and scientific events.
- Document your work and report to project coordinators and stakeholders.

Your profile:

- PhD degree in synthetic biology, biotechnology or related disciplines.
- Experience as experimental researcher in combination with modelling or data-driven methods is ideal. Previous experience as data steward, or previous work within NFDI Consortia is of advantage. Knowledge in automated workflows for SynBio research is advantageous.
- Interest in working with and for the digitalization of the ELM community.
- Self-driven and hands-on personality. Organization and prioritization skills.
- Very good communication skills in English.

We offer:

- An emergent research topic with multiple opportunities to contribute and interact with the growing community and contribute to its development at an early stage.
- Direct access to and high visibility in the SynBio and ELM networks at national and international level.
- An existing team with expertise and drive to move forward digitalization in ELM research. A well-structured on-boarding process and clear responsibilities.
- A community-oriented, multifaceted work with great scope for creativity.
- A highly professional and supportive working environment with an open and international culture.
- Strong support of training and career development towards an outstanding profile as data scientist in synthetic biology research.
- Flexible working hours and mobile working opportunity.
- A family-friendly working place.
- A EG 13 TV-L position (full time). A part time position is also possible.

The position is initially for 3 years.

Interested?

We look forward to your application! Please upload your CV and motivation letter, by**_ September 15th, 2026 _**via the online application system. For further information on this position, please contact INM Scientific Director Prof. Dr. Aránzazu del Campo (aranzazu.delcampo@leibniz-inm.de ).

The INM practices an open and appreciative corporate culture in which the existing diversity is promoted and lived. The institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy, and it provides offers for a better work-life balance, flextime, and mobile working. We promote professional opportunities for women and strongly encourage them to apply. Full time jobs can be generally divided. Severely disabled applicants with equal qualifications and aptitude will be given preferential consideration.

jobs.occupation: University Professor of Functional Genomics and Molecular Neurobiology (Professor/in - Hochschulen)
jobs.description:
Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region – home to the RMU Alliance formed by JGU, Goethe University, and TU Darmstadt – JGU can utilize its full potential and showcase its dynamic, innovative power. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching at JGU, in turn, paving the way for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its faculties and departments are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center, creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from all over the world.

The Institute of Developmental Biology and Neurobiology at the Faculty of Biology invites applications for the position of a

University Professor of Functional Genomics and Molecular Neurobiology

beginning at the earliest date possible. Salary grade W 2 LBesG | Civil servant (tenured)

Tasks and expectations:

We seek an outstanding candidate with a strong expertise in genetics and molecular biology, including the application of these approaches to the nervous system. Internationally recognised expertise and a strong track record of successfully securing external funding are required. Collaboration within the Faculty of Biology, the University Medical Centre, the Institute of Molecular Biology (IMB) and participation in current and future research consortia is expected.

The successful candidate will receive departmental positions and start-up funds and will be expected to establish an independent and internationally visible research program sustained by third party funding. Examples of further cooperation opportunities include: Institute of Quantitative and Computational Biosciences (IQCB) as well as collaborative research centres (e.g. CRC 1361 DNA Repair & Genome Stability; CRC 1551 Polymer Concepts in Cellular Function), the Research Unit FOR 5289 (From Imprecision to Robustness in Neural Circuit Assembly), or the Research Training Groups 4R (R-Loop Regulation in Robustness and Resilience) and GenEvo (Gene regulation in Evolution), the Carl-Zeiss-funded project for Interactive Bio-materials for Neural Regeneration and profile areas such as ReALity (Resilience - Adaptation - Longevity) or the Centre of Healthy Aging (further details here). The Rhine-Main Neuroscience Network (rmn²) offers further collaboration opportunities within the Rhine Main region.

Finally, the successful candidate will teach practical and theoretical courses in genetics, molecular biology and neurobiology at the Bachelor’s and Master’s level. We seek to increase the number of courses taught in English. Teaching is conducted in English and, in the basic Bachelor modules, in German. Applicants are therefore expected to be proficient in English and German. German language skills need to be acquired within five years of appointment. Participation in academic service is expected.

Requirements:

- In addition to the general requirements according to public services law, applicants must meet the recruitment requirements stipulated in Section 49 of the Hochschulgesetz of Rhineland-Palatinate. 
- In addition to the doctorate, a demonstration of excellent academic achievements is required. 

The state of Rhineland-Palatinate and JGU are committed to close personal mentoring of students and expect teaching staff to have a strong presence on campus. A cooperative, team-oriented and proactive work attitude, strong communication skills, and the willingness to assume responsibility – including further professional development in accordance with JGU’s leadership guidelines – is also expected.

Commitments of JGU:

JGU firmly supports making family and career compatible and promotes its employees’ further professional development. JGU welcomes qualified applications from people from diverse backgrounds. JGU aims to increase the number of women in research and teaching and therefore encourages female researchers to apply.

Candidates with severe disabilities or with equivalent status (as defined by section 2 subsection 3 of the Ninth Book of the Social Code, SGB IX) and appropriate qualifications will be given priority.

Please upload your complete application information and documents (CV, references, diplomas and certificates, as well as lists of publications and teaching activities, funding record, current research and future research plans, teaching concept) no later than September 30, 2026 via our portal with the following link: (https://berufungsportal.uni-mainz.de/datenabfrage/Genomics_Neurobiology)

https://berufungsportal.uni-mainz.de/datenabfrage/Genomics_Neurobiology (https://berufungsportal.uni-mainz.de/datenabfrage/Genomics_Neurobiology)

The interview symposium is tentatively planned for November 2026.

For questions and further information, please contact the chairperson of the search committee Prof. Martin Heine (marthein@uni-mainz.de).

Information on data protection: https://karriere.uni-mainz.de/en/#hinweise-zum-datenschutz (https://karriere.uni-mainz.de/en/#hinweise-zum-datenschutz)

jobs.occupation: Professorship in One Health, Animal Hygiene and Animal Disease Control (W3) (Professor/in - Hochschulen)
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine seeks to fill the mentioned above professorship at the earliest opportunity:

Academic context
Founded in 1409, the University of Leipzig is one of Germany's largest, most research-intensive and leading medical universities. It offers a dynamic and international working environment as well as attractive and diverse career opportunities in research, teaching, transfer, infrastructure and administration. The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine serves as a centre for interdisciplinary research in the fields of animal health, veterinary public health, public health and One Health.

The Institute of Animal Hygiene and Public Veterinary Services is a member of the Centre for Veterinary Public Health at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine. It has modern BSL-2 (Biosafety Level 2) laboratory facilities, an interdisciplinary research environment and a wide-ranging international network.

Future Duties
The professorship is responsible for independently representing the field of animal hygiene and animal disease control in teaching [in accordance with § 32 "Animal husbandry and animal hygiene" and § 39 "Animal disease control and infectious disease epidemiology" of the Ordinance on the Licensing of Veterinarians (Verordnung zur Approbation von Tierärztinnen und Tierärzten – TAppV)], research and services. In the subject of animal disease control, teaching is carried out in cooperation with the Centre for Infectious Diseases (Zentrum für Infektionsmedizin – ZIM). The professorship is also responsible for managing the Institute of Animal Hygiene and Veterinary Public Health.

The professorship is expected to strengthen the faculty's research profile, especially the One Health approach, and to focus on the rapid detection and containment of infectious diseases in animals, animal epidemics and zoonoses (Pandemic Preparedness). Compatibility and collaboration in the research priorities of the faculty (www.vetmed.uni-leipzig.de/forschung/forschungsschwerpunkte) and university (www.uni-leipzig.de/en/research/research-profile/strategic-orientation-of-our-research; www.uni-leipzig.de/en/newsdetail/artikel/strategic-research-profiling-leipzig-university-designates-eleven-emerging-fields-along-the-leipzig-way-2025-12-17) and the development of interdisciplinary and international clusters are expressly desired.

A teaching and research concept demonstrating the relevance of the planned projects to the research priorities of the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and other university institutions should be submitted with the application.

Requirements
In addition to in-depth knowledge of classical animal hygiene combined with modern, technology-based strategies for disease control, outstanding research and publication achievements, particularly in the fields of animal hygiene and/or infection epidemiology, experience in teaching and the successful acquisition of competitive third-party funding, especially international joint research projects are expected. Extensive experience in teaching and postgraduate continuing education and training, experience in personnel management and development are required. Proof of a veterinary licence and approval as a veterinary specialist for animal hygiene or in a relevant field, as well as proof of a postdoctoral qualification or equivalent achievements, must be provided.

The job holder’s rights and obligations are regulated by the Saxon Higher Education Act (SächsHSG) and the Saxon Service Regulations for Higher Education Institutions (HSDAVO). Applicants must meet the requirements of § 59 SächsHSG.

Research, teaching, transfer, infrastructure and administration require a diversity of perspectives. The university is therefore committed to diversity and equal opportunities. We welcome your application, regardless of gender, nationality, religion, cultural and social background, age or sexual orientation. The university aims to increase the proportion of women in academia and therefore expressly encourages qualified women to apply.

Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de.

Please apply in English by 17 September 2026 exclusively via Leipzig University’s recruitment portal (http://www.uni-leipzig.de/berufungen)

Making displays foldable? Helping hearts beat with medical innovations? Or breathing new life into precious metals? As a family-owned global technology group we help our customers to always being one step ahead.

Together we improve lives. At Heraeus Medevio, we bring lifesaving and life-changing medical devices to market through partnerships with medical device manufacturing companies. Sound Propagation, Resonance & Biofouling Prevention

HASYTEC (Ultrasonic Tech GmbH, part of the ERMA TECH Group) develops and markets highly innovative ultrasonic technology that prevents biofouling on fluid-carrying surfaces. Our systems protect more than 300 ships, offshore platforms, and maritime installations worldwide against barnacles, algae, and mussels—efficiently, sustainably, and with minimal maintenance.

To strengthen our development team, we are looking for an Ultrasonic Acoustics Engineer who is passionate about understanding sound propagation, resonance behaviour and ultrasonic systems in complex maritime structures.

This is not a standard engineering position.

PhD Candidate (f/m/x) in Ophthalmic Epidemiology
Code: 1547/2026/5

full-time, 3 years, extension possible
Site: Bonn

The German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is a globally leading, internationally oriented research institution dedicated to discovering new approaches for the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. Conduct research in ophthalmic epidemiology of aging in humans, with a focus on age-related macular degeneration. In particular, we expect you to:

Perform integrative analyses combining multi-omics data with eye imaging data
Contribute to ophthalmic data collection and processing
Contribute to omics data processing, statistical analyses, and the preparation of manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals
Present research findings at national and international conferences
Actively participate in project-related meetings, documentation, and reporting of project progress
Contribute to ongoing projects within the group and develop independent research ideas

A Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field, such as epidemiology, bioinformatics, medicine, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline
A genuine interest in scientific research and quantitative analysis
Strong proficiency in written and spoken English
Statistical knowledge and experience with programming in R
Experience with epidemiological research or large-scale observational studies, particularly involving omics and eye imaging data, including the application of machine learning methods for pattern recognition and predictive modeling is desirable but not a prerequisite
Strong analytical skills, independent and critical thinking, and attention to detail
Flexibility, strong interpersonal skills, and enjoyment of working in an interdisciplinary and international team
Proficiency in written and spoken German

Your role in Cutting-Edge Research

The PhD project will be supervised by Dr. Dr. Petra Larsen, scientific lead of the ophthalmic epidemiology team. The research is embedded in the large population-based Rhineland Study, a comprehensive long-term cohort investigating determinants of brain health. We are seeking an enthusiastic and ambitious early-career researcher (f/m/x) with a strong interest in investigating multi-omic and eye imaging signatures in the context of age-related macular degeneration.

The Ophthalmic Epidemiology research team investigates deep phenotyping of retinal ageing, preclinical changes and disease, as well as the comprehensive assessment of risk factors driving the onset and progression of both preclinical and clinical disease. These include genetic, molecular and environmental factors.

The PhD thesis will focus on the relationship between ageing and age-related macular degeneration and encompass the full breadth of scientific work, including the development and implementation of study protocols, coordination and supervision of data collection, and data analysis and publication.

The project will leverage data from the Rhineland Study, a deeply-phenotyped, large-scale population-based cohort study. Available data include comprehensive multi-omics data, including (epi)genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics; eye imaging data, advanced MRI data as well as extensive behavioral and clinical data, including cognitive and neurological assessments, cardiovascular assessments, medical history, and medication use. The study currently includes over 14,000 individuals, of whom more than 6,000 already have longitudinal data. Additional baseline and follow-up data collection is ongoing.

jobs.description:
About us The European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH
is a joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon, and NXP. For the
first time, TSMC, the global technology leader, is establishing a
semiconductor fabrication plant in the heart of Europe, offering
leading-edge manufacturing technologies for next-generation
semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared commitment to
strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For our future fab
in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and dedicated:
Senior HR Specialist - Apprenticeship & Vocational Training (m/f/d)
Are you ready to strategically and pedagogically lead the end-to-end
apprentice journey for Europe's newest, most advanced semiconductor
facility? As a Senior HR Specialist - Apprenticeship & Vocational
Training (m/f/d) at ESMC in Dresden, you will move beyond standard
administration to drive collaborative success across all core phases
of our technical vocational education. You will be the architect of
our future talent pipeline— managing employer branding at schools,
coordinating dual-training plans, mentoring Gen-Z apprentices, and
ensuring legal compliance. Fitting into our fast-paced greenfield
environment, this role offers a unique opportunity to shape the next
generation of microtechnology and industrial specialists from the
ground up! Tasks Talent Attraction & Recruitment: Design and execute
targeted school marketing strategies, represent ESMC at career fairs,
manage the applicant pipeline, conduct interviews, and issue
apprenticeship contracts. Onboarding & Pastoral Care: Serve as the
primary point of contact and dedicated mentor for future apprentices,
coordinating orientation phases and providing continuous coaching.
Training Curriculum Coordination: Design dual-training plans, manage
internal rotations across manufacturing departments, and coordinate
closely with local vocational schools (Berufsschulen).
Train-the-Trainer Support: Provide ongoing pedagogical and structured
guidance to our operational Fab trainers on the manufacturing floor.
Legal Compliance: Ensure full operational compliance with the German
Vocational Training Act (BBiG), the Youth Employment Protection Act
(JArbSchG), and other relevant educational laws. Key Stakeholder
Management: Build and maintain excellent collaborative relationships
with the local Works Council (Betriebsrat/JAV), vocational schools,
and local chambers (IHK). Graduation & Placement: Coordinate final
exam preparations, align with department managers to map out
post-graduation career pathways, and handle transition contract
processes. Profile Must-Have: Certifications: Holder of the AdA-Schein
(AEVO / Ausbildereignungsprüfung)—the mandatory qualification to
train apprentices in Germany. Education: Academic degree (B.Sc./M.Sc.)
or certified technical expert background (Staatlich geprüfter
Techniker) with a verified trainer/tester license. Experience: 5+
years of professional experience managing vocational training programs
within a technical, manufacturing, or industrial environment (e.g.,
semiconductor, automotive, automation, or chemical industries).
Regulatory & Institutional Knowledge: Strong, practical experience
working successfully with the IHK and a deep understanding of German
legal frameworks (BBiG, JArbSchG, and BetrVG). Languages: Fluent
German (C1/C2) is mandatory for official communications with
authorities, schools, and parents. Strong English skills (B2/C1) are
required for internal collaboration in our international corporate
environment. Pedagogical Drive: Exceptional communication skills with
the ability to motivate, resolve conflicts, and guide Gen-Z young
adults through their personal and professional development.
Nice-to-Have: Familiarity with cleanroom environments, semiconductor
fab safety regulations, and the technical demands of Microtechnology
(Mikrotechnologe/In). Experience setting up apprenticeship structures
in a fast-growing, ramp-up corporate environment. We offer Security &
Perspective: A permanent employment contract and career advancement
opportunities in one of Europe's leading semiconductors fabs. Company
Pension Plan & Financial Benefits: We support your financial
well-being with our robust company pension plan. As an ESMC employee,
you also benefit directly from TSMC’s performance through an
exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). Relocation Support for
Dresden: Moving for us? We’ll provide you with all the support you
will need for your relocation and your start in Dresden. Training &
Development: At the TSMC Newcomer Training Center, gain a deeper
understanding of the processes involved in operating complex
semiconductor equipment through unique hands-on training, while you
continuously expand your knowledge. Health & Well-Being: An annual
budget for your health and well-being (e.g., for sports classes,
massages, or relaxation) helps you stay fit. Meals & Transportation:
Enjoy a daily meal allowance as well as a subsidized public
transportation (e.g., for the Deutschlandticket). Additional contact
details Please apply with your English resume.

Work in a highly international environment with colleagues across the

Participate in global projects and cross-functional collaboration.
